intro.summary: Build a tool that opens a text file, counts its words, and copies the result to the clipboard. You only need LIMEN's platform module.
prepare.heading: 1. Set up the project
prepare.body: Complete the first window tutorial. Create a text-counter directory next to my-window and copy build.hxml and the same native files into it. Both project folders sit directly inside Limen.
source.heading: 2. Add the program
source.body: Save the code as text-counter/Main.hx. The app uses the window title to show instructions and the word count.
try.heading: 3. Build and try it
try.step.1: Create a UTF-8 file named sample.txt containing Hello from Limen.
try.step.2: Open a terminal in text-counter, run haxe build.hxml, then run hl main.hl. If you copied the bundled Windows runtime, use .\hl.exe main.hl.
try.step.3: Click the app window, press O, and select sample.txt. The title should show 3 words.
try.step.4: Press <kbd>C</kbd>, open a text editor, and paste the result. Also try opening an empty file and clicking Cancel in the file picker.
explain.heading: How it works
explain.step.1: Platform.pollEvent reads key presses and close requests. scanCode identifies the physical key, and keyRepeat lets you ignore auto-repeat. See the SDL scancode reference for key codes.
explain.step.2: FileDialog.openFile returns its result asynchronously. The callback puts it into a thread-safe queue, and the main loop reads the file and updates the title.
explain.step.3: File.getContent reads the entire small UTF-8 file. The \s+ pattern splits the text on runs of whitespace. Clipboard.setText writes the result to the system clipboard.
extend.heading: Make it your own
extend.body: Start by showing the file length alongside the word count. Then enable allowMultiple: true and add up the counts across all returned paths. For large files, try reading line by line.
